question: What is the primary mode of transmission for sexually transmitted infections?
explanation: Sexually transmitted infections are primarily spread through intimate mucosal contact during unprotected sexual intercourse. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h1)

question: How do bacterial and viral sexually transmitted infections fundamentally differ in clinical management?

options.A: Bacterial pathogens require lifelong daily antivirals, whereas viral pathogens respond instantly to single-dose antifungals
options.B: There is no clinical difference in how healthcare providers treat bacterial versus viral pathogens
options.C: Bacterial infections are typically curable with antibiotics, whereas viral infections are managed rather than cured
options.D: Viral infections require surgical intervention, while bacterial infections resolve spontaneously without treatment

explanation: Bacterial cellular structures respond well to specific antibiotics leading to a cure, whereas viruses integrate into host cells and require lifelong management or vaccination prevention. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which STI type is least effectively prevented by latex condoms because transmission occurs via uncovered skin-to-skin contact?
explanation: Skin-to-skin contact infections like human papillomavirus and herpes can infect areas outside the barrier coverage zone of a standard condom. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: A patient asks if female condoms offer any distinct advantage over male latex condoms. What is the correct nursing response?

options.A: Female condoms require no lubrication or careful placement during insertion
options.B: Female condoms eliminate all risks of skin-to-skin viral transmission entirely
options.C: Female condoms grant the receiving partner independent control over barrier protection
options.D: Female condoms are completely reusable across multiple sexual encounters

explanation: The internal pouch design allows the female partner to initiate and maintain barrier protection without relying on partner compliance regarding male condoms. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: When is the Human Papillomavirus vaccine ideally administered for maximum clinical efficacy?

options.A: Exclusively during the third trimester of pregnancy
options.B: Immediately following a confirmed diagnosis of genital warts
options.C: Before the onset of sexual activity
options.D: Only after a patient reaches forty years of age

explanation: Immunization yields the highest protection when given before an individual has any potential exposure to the virus through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the critical time window for initiating Post-Exposure Prophylaxis following a potential HIV exposure?
explanation: Post-exposure medications must be started promptly—ideally within 72 hours—to prevent the virus from establishing a permanent systemic infection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: What laboratory method is considered the gold standard for detecting chlamydia and gonorrhea due to its exceptional sensitivity?
explanation: Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests amplify genetic sequences, allowing accurate detection of even tiny amounts of bacterial DNA in clinical specimens. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: A pregnant woman attends her first antenatal care clinic. Why is routine STI screening initiated immediately during this visit?

options.A: To prevent vertical transmission of infections to the developing fetus
options.B: To calculate the precise basal metabolic rate of the mother
options.C: To determine the exact biological sex of the unborn child
options.D: To diagnose gestational diabetes mellitus in the first trimester

explanation: Early screening allows timely treatment of maternal infections, preventing catastrophic congenital complications and intrapartum transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary rationale for utilizing syndromic management in certain healthcare settings?

options.A: It guarantees absolute identification of the exact viral strain causing the disease
options.B: It serves as a replacement for surgical removal of infected tissues
options.C: It completely eliminates the possibility of developing antimicrobial resistance
options.D: It provides immediate treatment based on symptom clusters when laboratory tests are unavailable

explanation: Syndromic management ensures patients receive treatment on the day of presentation rather than waiting weeks for remote laboratory results. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice when treating bacterial sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Stopping medication immediately as soon as initial symptoms disappear
options.B: Completing the entire prescribed course of oral antibiotics
options.C: Abstaining from sexual intercourse during the treatment window
options.D: Treating sexual partners simultaneously to prevent reinfection

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early breeds resistant strains and leads to treatment failure; patients must finish the entire prescribed course. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why is partner notification considered an indispensable component of successful STI treatment programs?

options.A: It interrupts community transmission cycles and prevents reinfection of the index patient
options.B: It eliminates the need for any pharmacological interventions
options.C: It generates revenue for community laboratory testing facilities
options.D: It provides legal documentation for mandatory courtroom litigation

explanation: Without treating exposed partners, the index patient faces immediate reinfection upon resuming sexual activity with untreated contacts. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h6)

question: What distinguishes provider referral from patient referral in contact tracing?

options.A: Trained healthcare staff notify partners directly while maintaining patient confidentiality
options.B: Public announcements are published in local newspapers with patient names
options.C: Law enforcement officers arrest partners who fail to visit the clinic
options.D: The infected patient handles all communication without any clinical support

explanation: Provider referral places the burden of contact tracing on trained clinic staff, protecting patient privacy while ensuring exposed partners get care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h6)

question: How does establishing a non-judgmental, confidential environment directly impact STI prevention outcomes?

options.A: It legally exempts patients from paying hospital user fees and pharmacy charges
options.B: It encourages vulnerable patients to seek early testing and adhere to treatment plans
options.C: It automatically cures chronic viral infections without medication
options.D: It prevents healthcare workers from documenting vital signs accurately

explanation: Stigma drives patients away from clinics; creating a safe space ensures individuals feel secure enough to seek timely diagnosis and care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h7)

question: A patient diagnosed with a bacterial STI appears visibly distressed and fearful of social judgment. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Publicly reprimand the patient regarding their lifestyle choices
options.B: Delay all medical treatment until the patient stops crying
options.C: Inform family members immediately without patient consent
options.D: Provide empathetic, confidential counseling in a private setting

explanation: A supportive and private approach builds trust, reduces anxiety, and fosters effective engagement in treatment and partner notification. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h7)
